Unlike 2D methods, it operates directly on volumetric datasets, and unlike JPEG-based approaches, it avoids the lack of straightforward 3D counterparts for quantization tables [S1, unofficial].

The claim consists of two parts: 1) The method operates directly on volumetric datasets, unlike 2D methods. The evidence states that the paper generalizes schemes to '3D volume data' and extracts vectors as shown in Figure 4 for the 3D case, implying direct operation on volumetric data compared to the 2D context mentioned earlier. 2) Unlike JPEG-based approaches, it avoids the lack of straightforward 3D counterparts for quantization tables. The evidence explicitly states: 'this is not the case for JPEG (for instance, the quantization tables of the DCT coefficients have no straightforward counterpart in the 3D case)'. This confirms that the proposed method (which is being generalized to 3D) does not suffer from this specific limitation that JPEG does.
